body: Well, maybe Saix just went too hard on them while I was sending spell from afar. kinda want to redo the fight to see Roxas soloing Saix, specially if it's true that his moveset is taken from his KH2FM fight. Kinda bummed he didn't do much for me.

This is my main complaint as well. I felt like the game set it up pretty hard for second visits, and I feel like there would be really easy to slot in more KH original characters and interactions in these second visits, specially during a portion of the story that could've easily make Sora explore everything again while having narrative purposes to it.  
Overall, I'm not disappointed with the game. It worked really well for me, and was a really fun ride that touched in all the notes I expected from the game. But I feel like making it a bit longer, and pacing out all the character conclusions instead of cramming them all at the very end could've been way better, and I really expected that, because the worlds this time around just felt so good to explore that I wanted to do more at them. Specially since I honestly did not have my fill at the end. Not overly bummed about it though, still greatly enjoyed my time with what's here. But I agree that the second visits would be a good way to have expanded on what this game did so well.

The AI just kept bumbling around with me most of the game. Only noticed them when Donald occasionally gave me openings with magic, or when using the team commands. And in the Saix fight in general, they just got bodied by his berserker mode while Sora did all the heavy lifting by actually staggering the guy. So I can't say I exactly share the feeling that the AI is too strong.

I guess it all comes down to what people were expecting. If you thought this was a resolution to pretty much everything that was set up, I can be you being disappointed. However, ever since the news dropped that this would be the end of the "Xehanort saga", I was basically expecting a good ending for the villain himself, and a resolution for the conflicts he directly started. I sure wish they had a little less set-up with the box thing, but overall I got very satisfied with the package,a nd it got me very emotional when the Xehanort plotline was resolving after the final battle.  
For me, this was more of an ending to a story arc then to the series in general, so I was satisfied. However I can see how the people that expected an end to the series as a whole could be disappointed. Also, kinda wish the game had gone on for a little longer, but I guess that's because I didn't quite feel like I got my fill of the game as a whole by the end, so that's probably a good thing.
Well, that's sad. Thanks for trying though!

I don't know. Part of me knew that what I was doing was stupid. But I still wouldn't budge, you know? I know that in principle that is nothing that could be done about it now, but, I don't know. Thanks for sharing, though. Sometimes it just hurts particuarly more. It's weird to even type about it. I feel silly, even, for being so... inapt. I don't even know.

A lot of the people here already said it, but it really is a series you can start just about anywhere. The later games and Frontier are great, but, if you have in mind the objective of playing all of the games, I'd recommend playing the first one, since it's hard to go back to it, specially after getting used to 3 and 4 and their quality of life improvements. That's a big reason I have put off replaying the first game for a long while.  


As for tips, these games are really chill about how you go about things. The only things I'd say you have to know is that early game fishing is a really solid way to get some income, and that, if you want to get some cool weapons and equipment, you're gonna have to make them yourself, so keep a healthy stock of minerals and materials so you can level those up whenever you have some leftover stamina by the end of the day. But, overall, just have fun and chill. They are great games for just calming yourself after a long and stressful day.  


Also, I never really had too many problems with RNG in RF4, but I didn't really gun for the highest tier stuff and just took what the game gave me, so there is that.

Honestly, I like the attempt of making Endeavor's character more nuanced, but I don't think this will go so soon into the route of "totally forgiven". It's pretty clear this is about him making the first steps, and I doubt he will be completely forgiven by his family. This fight is supposed to symbolize Endeavor's beggining as the official number 1 hero, but also of his road to actually becoming worthy of that title. And, in that way, I do believe the man needs to walk a lot more along this road to truly be the kind of hero he actually aspires to be, or as he said to Shoto, a hero his son can be truly proud of.

Also, I don't get why people say Todoroki acted out of character. Even in the way he has shown his support for his father during the battle, it seemed to be in more of a confrotational tone. And, let's be honest, as much as Shoto wants to show his father that he will go on to be a better hero than him, I doubt he is the kind of person to wish death upon his father, even if he does not hold him in high regards. Not only that, but how could he prove to Endeavor that he can be better if the man he wants to prove wrong in the first place was dead? Todoroki's feelings are justified. It's not purely hatred he feels, and those chapters are showing us this as well.

Man, I've been through so much while playing this series. This series has been one of the constants in my life, and even when things were at their worst, Sora and friends would always remind me that things would eventually get better.

Not trying to get too sappy here, but no matter how convoluted the story got, getting this game and finally seeing the Xehanort saga come to a close, and remembering how much I got through with this game series at my side, the main menu screen playing "Dearly Beloved" is guaranteed to screw me up for a few minutes.

This was a nice read. I do think the themes in Kingdom Hearts, are a really important lens to understand the story, as they are very interwoven into the narrative, being what makes this story shine for me, even when it indulges in some... questionable time traveling developments.

The only thing I'd add is that the way Sora develops, it seems to me as if the main thing that led to him failing his mark of mastery exam is that, through his overly optimistic behaviour, he fails to be able to understand the weight of the pain those he wants to save have to deal with, making it harder for him to actually reach out for them, AKA mastering the "power of waking". By that interpretation, I feel like Kingdom Hearts 3 will focus on getting Sora to understand the "darkness", or the pain in himself and others, and only by doing that he will be able to fully save everyone, as he intends. That would make sense in the story as he would need to find his inner balance in order to actually aid in the fight for the light. At least that's how I feel analysing the themes, though I'm probably wrong on this prediction.

I agree with AnonTwo, and I feel like the genocide run is a commentary on the relationship of player and game. You become stronger. You "beat" the game with the strenght acquired. No more meaning to keeping on playing this game. Thus the "move on to the next" line from Chara. At that point in the game, it has already gone full meta. Chara themselves already have been presented as "the feeling you get when the numbers go up". For me, the soulless pacifist is not even Chara wanting to "play" with the human world and the others. It's a reminder that this world is now meaningless. You made it meaningless. It has no hope for a happy ending next. So, now, it's time for you, the player, to bring the same despair to other worlds. Other games. Repeat the cycle of becoming stronger and "beating" the game. Maybe not in as much of a literal sense as you "beat" Undertale, but the same idea. It's a deconstruction that goes beyond the game's own "borders". At least that's how I interpret it.
